html:
The Great Surgun was the forced removal of hundreds of thousands of Armenians, Georgians and others from the Ararat valley and Nakhchivan to Iran by Shah Abbas I of Safavid Iran in 1604 and 1605.

Retreating before an Ottoman army, Abbas applied a scorched earth policy, burning towns and fields and driving the people south across the Aras River, where many drowned. Armenian merchants of Julfa were settled in a new quarter of his capital Isfahan, called New Julfa, which grew into a hub of a trading network reaching from Amsterdam to Manila. Thousands of others were settled in the provinces. The deportation left eastern Armenia with a reduced Armenian population for two centuries.
